### Summary
Stage 4 structured review (`reviews/workflow/mech-goal-sequence-20261019/cycle-000001/stage-04/revision-0001/review_findings.md`, workflow finding `mim-c01-s04-f003`) identified 19 mapped ingredient records whose `curation_history` timestamps are non-monotonic due to historical merge append order.

body:
Found reviewing #214.

The repo's own documented merge procedure — `.claude/skills/merge-ingredients/reference/matching-strategies.md:54-56` — is *"Mark source as REJECTED … Preserves audit trail"*, and the schema has `REJECTED: "Determined to be invalid or duplicate"` for exactly this. Two REJECTED tombstones already live in the mapped collection, so the pattern is in use.

`scripts/apply_microbedecoder_residual_merges.py` instead removes the source record outright. Synonyms and `preferred_term` are carried onto the target and `occurrence_statistics` were `0/0`, but the `notes` field is not — and that is where the upstream key lives:

    notes: Imported from microbedecoder (source_id=kgmicrobe.trait:2_dichloropropane)

Compare two records from the *same* `microbedecoder_residual_locant_fixed.tsv` batch after #211 and #214:

- `CHEBI:27789` (UNMAPPED_0722, **promoted**) → `notes: Imported from microbedecoder (source_id=kgmicrobe.trait:2_dichloroethane)`
- `CHEBI:142468` (UNMAPPED_0784, **merged**) → `notes: None`

So `kgmicrobe.trait:2_dichloropropane → CHEBI:142468` now exists nowhere in the data, while 826 other records carry their `kgmicrobe.trait` source_id. Same for `2_trichloroethane`, `1_sodium_chloride`, `1_sodium_lactate`, and the five re-routed in #214's second commit. MIM publishes to kg-microbe, so the trait id is the join key back to the source.

Related asymmetry, worth a decision rather than a fix: promoted records get an SSSOM row keyed on `preferred_term`, merged ones get none (SSSOM subjects are never synonyms — `reconcile_sssom.py:74-82`). A consumer resolving raw microbedecoder labels through the SSSOM resolves `2-dichloroethane` and silently misses `2-dichloropropane`. Defensible — the target is already mapped — but it means four rows of one manifest batch got two different treatments.

## Suggested fix

Either carry the source `notes`/source_id onto the merge target (e.g. as an additional evidence item or appended note), or tombstone as REJECTED per the documented procedure instead of deleting. Then make the merge helper and the skill doc agree, since they currently don't.
title: Merging deletes the source record instead of tombstoning it, dropping its kgmicrobe.trait source_id

body:
A root cause, found by an adversarial reviewer on #699 who noticed one instance and asked whether it was a pattern. It is.

4-Hydroxyphenylacetic acid has CAS RN `156-38-7`. Strip the hyphens and you get `156387` — and the record was once mapped to **`CHEBI:156387`, aspyrone**, an unrelated fungal metabolite. Swept across every mapped record's YAML (identifier, evidence, notes, curation_history):

| record | CAS RN | was mapped to | which is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Indolyl acetic acid | 87-51-4 | CHEBI:87514 | ethyl 2-hexenoate |
| 4-Hydroxyphenyl acetic acid | 156-38-7 | CHEBI:156387 | aspyrone |
| Phenyl acetic acid | 103-82-2 | CHEBI:103822 | LSM-15166 |
| Ethanol | 64-17-5 | CHEBI:64175 | a mannose tetrasaccharide |
| L-Cysteine HCl | 52-89-1 | CHEBI:52891 | QSY9 succinimidyl ester, a dye |
| DL-mevalonic acid | 150-97-0 | CHEBI:150970 | a sialylated oligosaccharide |
| Sodium succinate dibasic | 150-90-3 | CHEBI:150903 | a fucosyl trisaccharide |
| Na-pyruvate | 113-24-6 | CHEBI:113246 | a benzodioxinyl triazinone |
| Isovaleric acid / Na-L-lactate / Phenyl propionic acid | 503-74-2 / 867-56-1 / 501-52-0 | CHEBI:503742 / 867561 / 501520 | no such term |

**None is live.** Every one of the eleven mappings was later corrected, and a sweep finds **0** records today whose identifier equals a de-hyphenated CAS of their own.

**But the corrections left residue**, the same way the cadmium-nitrate names outlived the calcium-nitrate fix: the April `cbclaw_kg_microbe_sweep` enriched synonyms from the identifier it was about to reject, in the same run. For the eleven records:

- 3 had already had the residue retired in #699's first pass (found the long way round, by ChEBI label collision);
- **3 more still carried it live** — a sialyl-oligosaccharide's systematic name on DL-mevalonic acid, the QSY9 dye's on L-cysteine HCl, and three names including `Fuc(a1-3)[Glc(a1-4)]Gal` on disodium succinate. All five were published in the SSSOM `other` column. Retired in #699;
- 5 are clean.

## Still open

1. **Which importer did this, and is it still reachable?** I have the symptom and the history, not the code path. The mapped-to identifiers that *do not exist* (CHEBI:503742, 867561, 501520) say the value was never validated against ChEBI at write time, which narrows it.
2. **A guard.** The check is one line and has no legitimate false positive I can think of: a record's `CHEBI:` identifier digits must not equal any of its own CAS RNs with the hyphens removed. It passes today, which is the cheapest moment to pin it.
3. **The wider sweep this implies.** For every record whose history shows a corrected ontology id, are there live synonyms that ChEBI assigns to the *old* id and not the current one? #699 did this for ChEBI *labels* (34 hits, 13 unrelated compounds) and for these eleven by all names. It has not been done by all names across every remapped record.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01BP6MDZgidgzS79c75Ykhac
title: An importer read CAS numbers as ChEBI accessions: 11 records were mapped to CHEBI:<CAS with hyphens stripped>

body:
Found while promoting a rebuilt SSSOM. **The promotion was reverted; nothing was
published.**

`just publish-sssom` reports a clean diff — 2,995 rows, `+0`, zero added, removed,
re-spelled or predicate-flipped — and passes every gate. It looks like the safest
possible promotion. It is not: it would delete **57% of the synonyms the SSSOM
publishes to KGX**.

```
published (in repo)   16,195 synonym tokens over 2,995 rows
fresh rebuild           7,002 synonym tokens over 2,995 rows
loss                    9,193  (57%), across 1,545 rows
```

`other` is the column kg-microbe merges into the ontology entity's synonyms
(`consolidate_chemical_mappings.py`, MIM#403), so those tokens are KGX synonyms.

Concretely, `MIM:~28R~29-lactate` -> CHEBI:16004:

```
published:  (2R)-2-hydroxypropanoate|D-2-hydroxypropanoate|D-2-hydroxypropionate|D-lactate
rebuild:    D-lactate
```

The three lost tokens are ChEBI's own exact synonyms for CHEBI:16004. The record
`data/ingredients/mapped/(R)-lactate.yaml` carries exactly one synonym, `D-lactate`, and
its history shows it never carried more — so those labels were **never derivable from the
curated record**. They entered the published artifact through some historical enrichment
that is not in the current pipeline.

## The current pipeline cannot reproduce them

- `build_mim_ingredient_sssom.py` builds `other` from record synonyms plus the kg-microbe
  dictionary. It is not the source of these.
- `review_sssom_synonyms.py` *identifies* the gap — 1,492 `SYNONYM_ENRICH` rows — but
  only stamps `validation_method` via `_write_sssom_inplace`. It never writes `other`.
- Applying every one of its 3,119 candidate labels still leaves **6,074 tokens
  unaccounted for**.
- `apply_synonym_review.py` (MIM) enriches records from the local chebi.db and would add
  469.

So build + both enrichment paths together reconstruct roughly half of what is published.

## Why the guard did not catch it

`publish_sssom.py` gates identity changes — added / removed rows, subject re-spellings,
predicate flips — and reports other columns only as a count of rows changed:

```
Other columns changed on surviving rows (reported, not gated):
    other    1672
```

"1,672 rows changed" is equally consistent with adding a synonym to each and with
deleting six from each. The direction is exactly the information a reader needs and the
only thing the line omits.

## Suggested

1. **Report direction, not just incidence.** `other N` should read as tokens gained /
   lost, and a large net loss should gate rather than report. Same argument as #416: a
   net number is blind to churn, and here even the incidence count is blind to sign.
2. **Decide where ontology synonyms live.** Either the builder emits them (making the
   artifact reproducible, which is the point of having a generator), or they are curated
   onto records so the record stays the source of truth. Today they live only in the
   published file, which is the one place nothing can regenerate.
3. Until then the SSSOM **cannot be safely rebuilt-and-republished**, which is worth
   stating plainly next to `reconcile_sssom.py`'s existing "no full generator" note —
   that note is about `validation_method` and per-row `source`, and this is a much
   larger hole in the same wall.
title: A clean-looking SSSOM rebuild silently deletes 57% of the synonyms published to KGX

body:
Split out of #443's audit as the one subset that is **semantically** wrong rather than a display defect. Small and self-contained.

`d-` and `D-` denote different substances. A record named `Alpha-d-glucose` is, read literally, asserting the wrong stereoisomer. The other 148 casing defects in #443 are ugly; these 8 are wrong.

## The cohort

| stem | `preferred_term` | grounded to |
|---|---|---|
| `Alpha-d-glucose` | `alpha-D-Glucose` ✓ | `CHEBI:17925` alpha-D-glucose ✓ |
| `N-acetyl-d-glucosamine` | `N-Acetyl-D-glucosamine` ✓ | **`CHEBI:8006` Peptidoglycan(N-acetyl-D-glucosamine)** ✗ |
| `Na-l-lactate` | `Na-L-lactate` ✓ | `CHEBI:232798` sodium L-lactate ✓ |
| `Hydroxy-l-proline` | `Hydroxy-L-Proline` ✓ | `CHEBI:18095` trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline ✓ |
| `3-beta-d-glucan` | `3-beta-d-glucan` ✗ | `CHEBI:37671` (1->3)-beta-D-glucan ✓ |
| `Beta-d-glucose` | `Beta-d-glucose` ✗ | `CHEBI:15903` beta-D-glucose ✓ |
| `6-deoxy-d-galactose` | `6-deoxy-d-galactose` ✗ | `CHEBI:2179` D-fucopyranose ✓ |
| `4-methylumbelliferone_Beta-d-glucuronide` | `4-methylumbelliferone Beta-d-glucuronide` ✗ | `CHEBI:1904` 4-methylumbelliferone beta-D-glucuronide ✓ |

Two separate defects, and the split matters:

- **4 records** (top block) already have a correct `preferred_term`; only the **filename stem** is lowercase. Cosmetic, and gated on #443's cross-repo rename decision.
- **4 records** (bottom block) have the defect in `preferred_term` itself. Fixable **now**, without touching a filename or retiring a CURIE.

## The real bug: `N-acetyl-d-glucosamine` is grounded to a peptidoglycan residue

```
record  -> CHEBI:8006    'Peptidoglycan(N-acetyl-D-glucosamine)'
correct -> CHEBI:506227  'N-acetyl-D-glucosamine'
           "The D isomer of N-acetylglucosamine."
```

`CHEBI:8006` is the residue *within a peptidoglycan polymer*, not the free sugar. As a growth-medium ingredient this is a carbon source supplied as the free monosaccharide, so the mapping names a different substance.

Nothing catches it: the label contains the string `N-acetyl-D-glucosamine`, so a substring or token-overlap check passes, and the record is internally self-consistent. That is the #324 shape — *"internally self-consistent so no existing check catches it"*.

Worth checking whether `CHEBI:28009` `N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosamine` is the better target if the source material specifies the anomer; `CHEBI:506227` is the safe unspecified-anomer choice.

## Suggested

1. Re-ground `N-acetyl-d-glucosamine` to `CHEBI:506227`, with a `CORRECTED` curation_history entry. Independent of everything else here.
2. Fix `preferred_term` on the 4 records where it carries the defect — no filename change, no CURIE retired.
3. Leave the 4 stem-only cases to #443's rename decision.
4. Consider a guard: a `preferred_term` whose stereodescriptor case disagrees with its own `ontology_label`'s would have caught all 4 of (2) and is cheap to assert.
title: 8 records carry a lowercase stereodescriptor; one of them is grounded to the wrong compound

body:
Found while fixing #502.

Moving curation-note filtering into MIM shared synonym policy exposed a separate pre-existing SSSOM issue: `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` still has 66 `other` tokens across 50 rows where the entire token is a parenthetical source fragment, matching `^\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$`. The flat lookup exporter already treats these as non-resolving detritus, so `docs/data/label_index.csv` refuses to publish them; final SSSOM should make the same decision.

Examples from the current published SSSOM:

- `MIM:2-mercaptoethanesulfonate` -> `(sodium salt)`
- `MIM:Agar` -> `( Noble)`, `(alternative)`, `(for solid medium)`
- `MIM:84_GL_NaHCO3_Solution` -> `(5% w/v solution)`, `(after autoclaving)`
- `MIM:Biotin` -> `(alternative)`

Scope: only whole-token parentheticals are suspect here. Real labels with internal parentheticals, such as `MOPS buffer (SIGMA)` and `(R)-lactate`, must continue to publish.

A fix probably needs both sides:

1. In MIM, remove or retag the source synonym rows that are pure parenthetical notes.
2. In culturebotai-claw, teach `scripts/build_mim_ingredient_sssom.py` to honor the same bare-parenthetical filter as the MIM shared synonym policy before filling `other`.
3. Regenerate `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` and only then promote a Rule J-style SSSOM gate from curation-note-only to the full non-resolving text policy.
title: SSSOM other still publishes bare parenthetical source fragments as synonyms

body:
Surfaced by #167, which made the collection headers honest: `data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml` now reports **1877 MAPPED + 2 non-MAPPED** against `total_count: 1879`. Previously the header claimed `mapped_count: 1877 / unmapped_count: 0` against 1879 records — self-inconsistent, so the 2 were invisible.

The 2 are `data/ingredients/mapped/Bacto_Soytone.yaml` and `data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_L-lactate.yaml`. Both have **two** problems.

## 1. `mapping_status: REJECTED` but filed under `mapped/`

Both carry `mapping_status: REJECTED` while living in `data/ingredients/mapped/` and appearing in `data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml`. Either the rejection should move them to `unmapped/`, or the status is wrong.

## 2. The record `identifier` contradicts its own `ontology_mapping`

Per `docs/CURIE_STANDARD.md`, in MIM the record `identifier` **is** the ontology mapping CURIE for a mapped record. Neither of these satisfies that:

| file | `identifier` | `ontology_mapping.ontology_id` | problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sodium_L-lactate.yaml` | `CHEBI:867561` | `CHEBI:232798` (sodium L-lactate) | identifier ≠ mapping; **and `867561` exceeds the `CHEBI: 300000` plausibility ceiling** in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, the signature of a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix |
| `Bacto_Soytone.yaml` | `CHEBI:8150` | `FOODON:03315720` ("vegetable protein, hydrolyzed") | identifier ≠ mapping, and the **prefixes disagree** — identifier says CHEBI, mapping says FOODON |

The `CHEBI:232798` and `FOODON:03315720` mappings both look correct; it is the `identifier` that is stale or wrong in each case.

## Why the plausibility gate did not catch `CHEBI:867561`

The id↔label gate validates `(ontology_id, ontology_label)` pairs. The bogus value is in the `identifier` field, which is not part of a validated pair — so an out-of-ceiling CHEBI can sit in the primary key indefinitely. Worth considering whether `identifier` should be range-checked too, given that in MIM it is by definition an ontology CURIE.

## Related

`Bacto_Soytone`'s mapping target `FOODON:03315720` is the same term already carried by `Phytone` and `Soya_Pepton` (see the duplicate-primary-key item in `NEXT_TASKS.md`), so resolving this should be coordinated with that dedup.
title: REJECTED and PENDING_REVIEW records sit in data/ingredients/mapped/ — 29 of them now

body:
Found reviewing #227. Applies to #214's 9 merges as well, and the new `merge_unmapped_into_mapped.py` guarantees it repeats.

## The regression

A merge deletes the UNMAPPED record and adds its raw label as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym on the target. By design it adds **no SSSOM row** — SSSOM subjects are `preferred_term`s of MAPPED records, never synonyms (`reconcile_sssom.py:74-82`), so adding one would be reported ORPHAN.

But `docs/data/{all,mapped,unmapped}_ingredients.csv` have **no synonyms column**:

    identifier,ontology_id,preferred_term,mapping_status,ontology_label,ontology_source,mapping_quality,total_occurrences,media_count

So after a merge the raw label appears in **no flat artifact at all**. Only `docs/data/ingredients.json` (which has `synonyms`/`searchable`) and the YAML retain it.

## Failure scenario

A kg-microbe consumer joining raw ingredient strings against `docs/data/all_ingredients.csv` or `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`:

- **before** #227: `D-lactate` → `UNMAPPED_0654` — resolves to "known ingredient, not yet grounded"
- **after**: `D-lactate` → **nothing**

Record-level coverage went *up* (the label is now grounded to CHEBI:16004) while flat-surface coverage went *down*. That is the opposite of the intended effect, and it is invisible to every current gate: reconcile is GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0, roundtrip is clean, qc-duplicate-ids is clean.

Affected so far: 5 labels from #227 (`3-hydroxy 2-butanone`, `D-lactate`, `Iso-butanol`, `N-acetyl-neuraminic Acid`, `Trimethyleneglycol`) and 9 from #214 (`2-dichloropropane`, `1% Sodium Chloride`, `Peptones`, …).

## Options

1. **Add a synonyms column to `export_lists.py`** — smallest change, keeps SSSOM semantics intact, makes the CSVs self-sufficient for string resolution.
2. **Emit a synonym-subject SSSOM row** with a distinct predicate — richer, but needs `reconcile_sssom.py` and the invariant validator taught about non-preferred_term subjects, and a decision on the right predicate.
3. Accept it and document that raw-string resolution must go through `ingredients.json`.

Option 1 looks right. Whichever is chosen, a check that every `RAW_TEXT` synonym is resolvable from at least one published flat artifact would stop this recurring.

Related: #227, #214, #220.
title: Merging a raw label into an existing record removes it from every flat export and from SSSOM

body:
Found while migrating SSSOM `other` surface forms onto records (#520).

19 subjects in `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` do not correspond to any record
file, because the record was renamed after the row was published and the subject CURIE is
derived from the filename stem:

```
MIM:Bis~282-ethylhexyl~29phthalate
MIM:Calcium~282~29
MIM:L-~3B1-phosphatidylinositol_From_Glycine_Max_Soybean
MIM:Magnesium~282~29
MIM:Methyl_~28R~29-lactate
...
```

`MIM:` CURIEs are built by `build_mim_ingredient_sssom._mim_curie` as the stem with
non-URL-safe characters `~HEX`-escaped, and the note in `MEMORY`/`CURIE_STANDARD` that
they are "not rename-stable" is exactly this. `mappings/mim_curie_aliases.tsv` exists to
resolve renames, but these 19 are not in it.

Consequence for the #520 migration: those subjects carry **1,409 `other` tokens that
cannot be attributed to a current record**, so they are the one part of the artifact the
migration cannot move into curated data. They are neither confirmed redundant nor
confirmed unique — they are simply unattributable.

Two things worth doing:

1. Resolve the 19 through `mim_curie_aliases.tsv` (or confirm the records were merged
   away, in which case the rows are ORPHANs and `reconcile_sssom` should be seeing them —
   it currently reports 0, which is worth understanding on its own).
2. Once resolved, re-run
   `scripts/backfill_sssom_surface_forms.py` so their tokens get the same
   redundant/unique/damaged triage as the rest.

Not addressed in #522, which deliberately migrates only what it can attribute.
title: 19 SSSOM subjects have no record file after renames, stranding 1,409 other tokens

body:
`justfile:603`:

```
# Assert the published SSSOM satisfies the CURIE standard.
[group('QC')]
curie-validate:
    uv run python -m pytest tests/test_curie_normalizer.py -q --no-cov
```

The body runs unit tests against fixtures. It never reads `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`.

Measured on 2026-08-21, before PR #436: the recipe passed **19/19 green** while the published file carried **11 subjects that violate `curie.py`'s own `_CURIE_RE`** — unescaped parentheses, which the regex at `curie.py:67` rejects:

```
MIM:(-)-anisomycin
MIM:(R)-lactate
MIM:(S)-mandelic_Acid
MIM:Calcium(2)
...
```

`_CURIE_RE` is the very pattern `tests/test_curie_normalizer.py` exercises. The recipe tested the implementation and called it a check on the artifact.

Same class as the #178 / #179 / #180 / #188 / #189 thread: a guard that reports OK while checking nothing. It is also part of why #236 went unnoticed for as long as it did — the one recipe named after this exact property could not see it.

## Fix

Have the recipe read the artifact: assert every `subject_id` and `object_id` in the published TSV matches `_CURIE_RE`, then run the unit tests. PR #436 brought the violation count to 0, so the check can be added in enforcing mode immediately rather than report-then-enforce.

Worth also checking the sibling recipes for the same shape — a comment that promises an artifact check over a body that only runs unit tests.
title: just curie-validate claims to assert the published SSSOM but never opens it

body:
Two small correctness gaps in `scripts/aggregate_records.py`, both found during #167.

## 1. Silent data loss on a corrupt per-record file

`aggregate_individual_files` catches a per-file load exception, prints it, **skips the record**, and the script still `sys.exit(0)`. A single malformed YAML therefore drops an ingredient out of the aggregated collection while the command reports success.

Downstream this surfaces only as a bare `ingredient count mismatch (1879 vs 1878)` from `verify_roundtrip.py`, with the actual cause already gone from view. #167 stopped `just qc-roundtrip` from discarding the aggregator's stdout, so the diagnostic is at least visible now — but the exit code is still wrong.

**Fix:** exit non-zero when `errors` is non-empty (or add `--strict` and use it in the gate).

## 2. `unmapped_count` conflates REJECTED with UNMAPPED

The header is computed as:

```python
mapped_count = sum(1 for ing in ingredients if ing.get('mapping_status') == 'MAPPED')
unmapped_count = len(ingredients) - mapped_count
```

Anything not `MAPPED` is counted as unmapped. After #167 made the headers honest, `data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml` reads `unmapped_count: 2` — but those 2 records (`Bacto Soytone`, `Sodium L-lactate`) are `mapping_status: REJECTED`, not `UNMAPPED`. See #170.

The count is right; the label is wrong, and it is a field consumers can read.

**Fix:** count `UNMAPPED` explicitly and either add a `rejected_count` or drop records with other statuses from the arithmetic rather than folding them into `unmapped_count`.
title: aggregate_records.py exits 0 after skipping unloadable records; header conflates REJECTED with unmapped

body:
## Finding

Ten records whose **label explicitly names a counterion or says "salt"** carry a
mapping whose **recorded structure is a net-charged ion**. Seven are graded
`EXACT_MATCH` — the strongest identity claim available, asserting that a salt
*is* its anion.

| net charge | identifier | quality | label | term (verified OLS4) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| −2 | CHEBI:16810 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na2 alpha-ketoglutarate` | `2-oxoglutarate(2-)` |
| −2 | CHEBI:29988 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na-glutamate` | `L-glutamate(2-)` |
| −2 | CHEBI:30924 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na-tartrate` | `L-tartrate(2-)` |
| −1 | CHEBI:29032 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Ca-pantothenate` | `(R)-pantothenate` |
| −1 | CHEBI:35899 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Na-crotonate` | `crotonate` |
| +1 | CHEBI:46020 | **EXACT_MATCH** | `Tetramethyl ammonium` | (cation) |
| −2 | cas:12208-13-8 | FALLBACK_REGISTRY | `potassium hexahydroxoantimonate` | — |
| −1 | cas:207511-06-6 | NARROW_MATCH | `L-Malic acid disodium salt monohydrate` | — |
| +1 | cas:9067-32-7 | NARROW_MATCH | `Hyaluronic acid sodium salt from S. equi` | — |
| +1 | kgmicrobe.compound:… | CLOSE_MATCH | `Tetramethyl ammonium chloride` | — |

All five CHEBI labels above verified live against OLS4; none obsolete.

## Why these are not covered by the #213 convention

MIM deliberately grounds **bare anion labels** (`Fumarate`, `Citrate`, `Lactate`)
to the fully-deprotonated CHEBI class, and that is correct — a bare label carries
no counterion, and the anion is the species present at growth-medium pH.

These ten are a different case: the label **names the counterion**
(`Na2 …`, `Ca-…`, `… sodium salt`). Sodium glutamate and glutamate(2−) are
different substances with different formulas, masses and CAS numbers. So the
convention does not license `EXACT_MATCH` here, and the anion mapping — while a
reasonable *close/narrow* relation — overstates as identity.

Note also `Na-glutamate`: monosodium glutamate is the **mono**-anion salt, so
even the charge state of the current target is off by one.

## Detection

Mechanical and high-precision. Net charge must be computed across **both** InChI
layers — `/q` alone gives 119 false positives, because a neutral salt like AlCl3
is written `/q+3;;;/p-3`:

```python
net = sum(component /q charges) + /p          # non-zero  => recorded structure is an ion
defect = net != 0 and label names a counterion or "salt"
```

That narrows 119 → 40 → **10**, with no false positives in the 10 on inspection.

## Suggested action

Per record: either re-ground to a CHEBI salt term where one exists, or keep the
anion term and downgrade `mapping_quality` to `CLOSE_MATCH`/`NARROW_MATCH` with
the reason recorded. The `EXACT_MATCH` grade is the part that is indefensible.

Worth adding the check to the validation suite so a future promotion sweep
cannot reintroduce it.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the Claude research lane on `1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium_Lysine`
(CHEBI:61326 is the [C2mim]⁺ cation alone; the ingredient is a neutral salt),
then generalised repo-wide. Related: #312 (ledger triage), #309 (the two-lane
harness).
title: Salt-named records mapped EXACT_MATCH to the bare anion (10 records)

body:
`conf/id_label_targets.yaml` sets `max_accession: CHEBI: 300000`. The validator treats an id that **does not resolve locally AND sits above the ceiling** as "a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix".

During the microbedecoder onboarding (#193) that rule rejected 17 groundings as `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE`, and I acted on it — demoting all 17 to `UNMAPPED`. **That was wrong.**

## Verified against live OLS4

All 17 are **real, non-obsolete ChEBI terms with exactly the labels claimed**:

| id | label |
|---|---|
| `CHEBI:474053` | cefazolin |
| `CHEBI:759883` | colistin sulfate |
| `CHEBI:747005` | 1-chlorobutane |
| `CHEBI:495056` | gamma-cyclodextrin |
| …and 13 more | cefepime, cefixime, cefotiam, ertapenem, imipenem, gentamicin, netilmicin, polymyxin B, carbomycin, anisomycin, lysostaphin, 1-chloropropane, 4-nitrophenyl α-D-galactoside |

They fail only because the **local ChEBI sqlite build is stale** and cannot resolve them, and the ceiling then reclassifies the non-resolution as "foreign identifier".

## The heuristic is not worthless

Checked the same way, #170's `CHEBI:867561` (Sodium L-lactate's identifier) returns **NOT FOUND** from OLS4 — genuinely bogus, correctly caught. So the rule catches real problems; it just cannot distinguish "invalid id" from "valid id my local ontology copy predates".

## Why this matters beyond 17 records

ChEBI keeps minting accessions above 300000. As-is, this gate will reject **every future grounding to a recent ChEBI term**, and the failure presents as "foreign identifier" — which invites exactly the destructive response I took.

## Options

1. **Refresh the local ChEBI adapter** — addresses the root cause; the ceiling then only fires on ids that genuinely don't exist anywhere.
2. **Fall back to OLS4 before declaring ID_OUT_OF_RANGE** — a non-resolving id above the ceiling gets one live lookup before being called foreign. Slower, but it is the check that would have prevented this.
3. Raise the ceiling — cheapest, but it weakens the one signal that correctly caught #170.

(1) or (2). Related: #170, #193, #195.
title: The CHEBI accession ceiling mis-rejects valid recent terms — 17 false positives, verified against live OLS4

body:
Review finding on #211 ("Recover 22 free microbedecoder residual groundings orphaned by closed PR #201").

## The claim

#211's body states:

> 0/20 of the `residual_grounded` set and **2/4 locant fixes were present**.

## What is actually true

All **4** records in `microbedecoder_residual_locant_fixed.tsv` are still `UNMAPPED` on the #211 branch:

| identifier | record | target | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| UNMAPPED_0722 | `unmapped/2-dichloroethane.yaml` | CHEBI:27789 | promoted by #211 ✅ |
| UNMAPPED_0789 | `unmapped/3-trichloropropane.yaml` | CHEBI:34036 | promoted by #211 ✅ |
| UNMAPPED_0784 | `unmapped/2-dichloropropane.yaml` | CHEBI:142468 | **still UNMAPPED** ❌ |
| UNMAPPED_0786 | `unmapped/2-trichloroethane.yaml` | CHEBI:36018 | **still UNMAPPED** ❌ |

The last two were not "present" — their *targets* are present (`mapped/12-dichloropropane.yaml`, `mapped/112-trichloroethane.yaml`), which is precisely why `promote_resolved_unmapped.py` could not take them. Closed PR #201 handled them as **merges**: add the raw label as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym on the existing mapped record, drop the unmapped record, add no new SSSOM row.

## Why it matters

#211's "None collide with existing records" is what excluded them, but nothing in the PR records that they still need work. Once #211 merges, these two sit in the residual with no manifest row pointing at them and no open action — the same way PR #201's whole slice was lost.

Two further records are in the identical state and also came from #201: UNMAPPED_0721 `1% Sodium Chloride` → CHEBI:26710 and UNMAPPED_0634 `1 % Sodium Lactate` → CHEBI:75228.

## Verification

All four merge targets resolve in the local `chebi.db`; the two chloroalkane reconstructions were independently re-checked by enumerating every CHEBI label whose comma-split tail matches the raw fragment — `2-dichloropropane` maps only to the 1,2- constitution (CHEBI:142468 plus its (R)/(S)/rac stereo-children, so the stereo-parent is the correct choice) and `2-trichloroethane` only to CHEBI:36018.

## Fix

Apply the 4 merges in a follow-up stacked on #211, and correct the wording in #211's description.
title: PR #211 leaves 2 locant-fix records unhandled and mis-describes them as already present

body:
## Finding

Of **1,864** records graded `EXACT_MATCH`, **356** carry a CHEBI term whose
primary label equals neither the record's `preferred_term` nor any recorded
synonym. Resolving each against the local `chebi.db` synonym lists splits them
cleanly:

| | count | |
|---|---|---|
| justified by a ChEBI **synonym** | **297** | term is right, **grade is wrong** |
| matched by **nothing** in ChEBI (label or synonym) | **59** | needs individual review |

## The 297 are mis-graded by the schema's own definition

`mediaingredientmech.yaml` is unambiguous:

```yaml
EXACT_MATCH:    Direct exact match to ontology term
SYNONYM_MATCH:  Matches known synonym in ontology
```

A label matching a ChEBI *synonym* rather than the primary label is
`SYNONYM_MATCH` by definition. This is not a judgement call — it is 16% of all
`EXACT_MATCH` records disagreeing with the enum they use.

The grade is load-bearing: it is what tells a downstream consumer how much to
trust an identity assertion, and `EXACT_MATCH` is the strongest claim available.

## The 59 need review, and are not one thing

Sub-classes visible on inspection:

- **Genuine scope loss** — the label carries a qualifier the term does not:
  `b-Glucan from Oat` → `beta-D-glucan` (source lost),
  `amylopectin from maize` → `amylopectin`,
  `Acetate (carbon source)` → `acetate`,
  `Ammonium chloride (nitrogen source)` → `ammonium chloride`,
  `Alpha-Toxicarol (Dl)` → `Toxicarol` (racemate → unspecified).
- **A semantic error** — `Aromatic hydrocarbon` → `polycyclic arene`. Not a
  synonym relation in either direction: benzene is an aromatic hydrocarbon and
  is not polycyclic. The term is narrower than the label.
- **Trivial-vs-systematic naming**, arguably fine but not *exact*:
  `Butanol` → `butan-1-ol`, `2-Ethylhexanol` → `2-ethylhexan-1-ol`,
  `2-Piperidinone` → `piperidin-2-one`.
- **Formula-as-label**: `KNO2` → `potassium nitrite`, `NH42CO3` →
  `ammonium carbonate`. The formula is not a ChEBI string at all.
- **Misspellings that nonetheless resolved correctly**:
  `Pyromelitic acid` → `pyromellitic acid`, `Thioglycollic acid` →
  `thioglycolic acid`. Compound is right; `EXACT_MATCH` is not.

## Reproduction

```python
# for each EXACT_MATCH record with a CHEBI ontology_id:
#   skip if preferred_term or a recorded synonym == ontology_label (normalised)
#   else look up the term's synonyms in ~/.data/oaklib/chebi.db:
#     any match -> should be SYNONYM_MATCH   (297)
#     no match  -> review                     (59)
```

Normalisation is case- and punctuation-insensitive, so this does not flag mere
capitalisation differences.

## Suggested action

The 297 are a safe mechanical re-grade to `SYNONYM_MATCH` with a
`curation_history` entry — no ontology_id changes, no SSSOM object changes.
Note the SSSOM predicate may need review alongside it, since `skos:exactMatch`
rows resting on a synonym match are the same overstatement.

The 59 need per-record calls; the scope-loss and `Aromatic hydrocarbon` cases
are real defects, the naming-convention ones probably just want re-grading too.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the Claude research lane, which flagged `EXACT_MATCH` as
unsupportable on `1-naphtylacetic_Acid`, `5-Hydroxyoctanoate`, `Angustmycin` and
`Aluminium_Sulfate` independently, then generalised repo-wide against chebi.db.
Related: #309, #312, #315, #316.
title: 297 records graded EXACT_MATCH are synonym matches; 59 more match nothing in ChEBI

body:
## Finding

MIM applies a real, load-bearing convention when grounding bare anion labels:

> Ground a bare anion label (`Fumarate`, `Citrate`, `Lactate`) to the
> fully-deprotonated CHEBI class **where one exists**; otherwise to the
> bare-name class.

**It is written down nowhere.** A search across all `*.md` and `*.yaml` outside
`data/` for `bare anion` / `bare-name` / `fully deprotonated` returns one
unrelated hit in a 2026 batch-suggestions note. The convention exists only in
per-record `evidence.notes` on the records that already applied it, and in issue
#213 discussion.

A curator working the residual reconstructed it by reading 12 sibling records
and generalising — correctly, as it happens, but that is inference from
observed practice, not a documented rule. The next one may generalise it wrong.

## Why it matters more than a typical doc gap

The rule has a **per-record branch that is easy to miss**, and both sides of it
are currently live in the data:

- `Aspartate` → should be `CHEBI:29995 aspartate(2-)`; it is currently on
  `CHEBI:132943 aspartate`, a structure-free, definition-free class. The
  structural analogue `Glutamate` is already on `CHEBI:29987 glutamate(2-)`, so
  the data is internally inconsistent. 431 occurrences — the highest-traffic
  record found in the lane so far.
- `Ascorbate` → the bare-name class **is** correct here, because no
  `ascorbate(1-)`/`(2-)` term exists in ChEBI (verified: `CHEBI:22651`'s only
  child is `L-ascorbate`). Rewriting it to an `X(n-)` term would be wrong.

So a mass-application of "always use the deprotonated form" would fix Aspartate
and break Ascorbate, Succinate and Malate. The "where one exists" clause is the
whole rule, and it is exactly the part an undocumented convention loses.

A second consequence: `ols-label-exact-chebi` ranks **primary labels only**,
which is why `Aspartate` landed on the class in the first place — the matcher
cannot implement a convention nobody wrote down.

## Suggested action

Document it in `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` alongside the predicate semantics, with:

- the rule and its `where one exists` branch,
- how to test the branch (search ChEBI for `<label>(n-)`; check the bare-name
  class for structure/definition — a structure-free class is a signal, not a
  target),
- the worked examples on both sides (Aspartate vs Ascorbate),
- and the note that structure-free classes must **not** be chemistry-enriched
  (an enrichment pass copying `L-ascorbate`'s structure onto the `ascorbate`
  class would be a #316-style defect).

Related: #213, #312, #315, #316, #317.
title: The bare-anion grounding convention is undocumented; curators are inferring it from practice

body:
## Summary

CommunityMech is building ENVO-based cross-repo linking (its issue
[#30](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CommunityMech/issues/30)). The **media**
half now works — a community's `environment_term` is matched against CultureMech
`source_environment`, emitting `related_media` blocks keyed on a shared ENVO term
(CommunityMech PR #211). The **ingredient** half is blocked on one MIM-side
question: **what is the stable canonical ingredient CURIE that an external repo
should cite?**

This issue asks MIM to confirm that, and to confirm the durability of the ENVO
`environmental_context` field (added in #1) as the join key.

## What CommunityMech found looking at MIM

- MIM's canonical ingredient identity is **`MIM:<Ingredient_Name>`** — 2200
  subjects in `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`, with the `MIM:` prefix
  expanding to `.../data/ingredients/mapped/`, mapped to ontology terms
  (CHEBI/FOODON/…) via SSSOM. This matches `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` (the
  registry/identity-row pattern).
- Ingredient records under `data/ingredients/mapped/` carry
  `identifier: kgmicrobe.ingredient:…` / `CHEBI:…` and, where curated,
  `environmental_context[].environment_term` (ENVO). ~44 currently carry an
  ENVO context.
- The **`MediaIngredientMech:NNNNNN`** style id appears only in two `analysis/`
  reports (`merge_pattern_analysis.yaml`, `duplicates_and_variants.yaml`) and in
  **zero** canonical records or the unified mapping TSV.

The problem: **CommunityMech's schema references the last one.**
`RelatedIngredient.mediaingredientmech_id` has pattern `^MediaIngredientMech:\d{6}$`
— a scheme MIM does not use canonically — so there is no valid id for
CommunityMech to emit, and its 222 existing `related_ingredients` populate no id
at all.

## Asks (MIM-side confirmation, no code change strictly required)

1. **Canonical cross-repo id.** Confirm `MIM:<name>` is the stable identifier
   external repos should cite for an ingredient (as opposed to routing through the
   ingredient's `CHEBI:` mapping, or the legacy `MediaIngredientMech:NNNNNN`).
   If `MIM:<name>` labels are subject to renaming, is there a rename-stable
   surrogate?
2. **ENVO field durability + coverage.** Is `environmental_context` a maintained
   field going forward, and is broader population expected? Its coverage (~44
   ingredients) is what determines how much environment-based ingredient
   suggestion is possible downstream.
3. **CHEBI route.** For ingredients that `skos:exactMatch` a CHEBI term, is citing
   the `CHEBI:` id (which CommunityMech's `RelatedIngredient.chebi_term` already
   supports) an acceptable equivalent link? That would let CommunityMech link many
   ingredients today without waiting on id decisions.

## Downstream once confirmed

CommunityMech will align its schema (add `shared_environment_term` to
`RelatedIngredient`; correct the id field to match MIM's canonical scheme) and
extend its environment-based suggester to emit ingredient links. Tracked in
CommunityMech `NEXT_TASKS.md` §2c.

Context: CommunityMech PRs #210 (coverage dashboard) and #211 (media suggester).
title: Canonical ingredient CURIE for cross-repo citation (CommunityMech ENVO linking)

body:
Consolidated tracker for the microbedecoder residual after PRs #192/#195/#198/#202/#211. As of #211 there are **~583 `UNMAPPED_*` placeholder records** still unmapped (2,301 mapped total). This issue records what's left and how it breaks down, since the residual has been worked in slices.

## Known, scoped buckets (have a path)
- **~43 multi-component media / co-substrate labels** — researched with a decomposition strategy in #202 (`mappings/microbedecoder_residual_research_decomposition.tsv`): BHI, PYG/PYGS/GYPS/PYEG, TYGVS, rumen-fluid media, and H2+X / formate+X / alcohol+CO2 / glucose+X donor–acceptor pairs. Need a decompose / complex-medium curator pass; gaps flagged: rumen fluid (verify MICRO:0000520, #204), corn steep liquor, VFA mixture.
- **6 out-of-coverage antibiotics** (carbomycin, colistin sulfate, gentamicin, lysostaphin, netilmicin, polymyxin B) — OLS4-validated CHEBI terms absent from the local `chebi.db`; blocked on the upstream build (#200/#207).
- **7 already-mapped synonym-merges + RNA/Torula split** — #208.
- **sodium(+) scope/relabel** — #209.
- **keratin → Protein Ontology** (no CHEBI term).

## Larger remainder (no grounding pass yet)
- The bulk of the ~583 residual has not been through a normalized/fuzzy or deep-research grounding pass. Some are genuine net-new chemicals; a meaningful fraction are **isolation-category environment/host/food** rows (`#Soil`, `#Marine`, `#Feces`, `#Food production`, …) that should route to **ENVO/FOODON**, not the ingredient pipeline (~347 per the 2026-08-03 assessment), plus numeric/phenotype noise that should be dropped.

## Suggested next steps
1. Refresh `chebi.db` to unblock the 6 antibiotics (#200/#207).
2. Run the decomposition pass on the 43 blends (#202 table).
3. Route the isolation-category rows to ENVO/FOODON grounding (separate from ingredients).
4. Deep-research / normalized-fuzzy pass over the remaining net-new chemical candidates.

Related: #200, #202, #204, #207, #208, #209.
title: Tracking: remaining microbedecoder residual unmapped labels (~583 after #211)
